title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.intervention: Addition of rhenium (Re) to the alloy
recollection.structure: Likely a single-phase solid solution, possibly with altered microstructure due to Re addition
recollection.mechanism: Rhenium addition may improve irradiation resistance by stabilizing defect structures, reducing defect mobility, or altering the electronic structure to suppress damage accumulation
recollection.results: Probably observed improved irradiation resistance, such as reduced swelling, lower defect concentration, or enhanced mechanical properties under irradiation; quantitative results might include decreased dislocation loop density or improved hardness retention, but this is a guess.

score.note: The recollection identifies Re addition, but this is already explicit in the title and omits the He implantation conditions. It generically suggests a single-phase alloy and altered microstructure without recalling grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, or suppressed boundary bubbles. The proposed defect-based mechanism is broadly plausible but does not identify enhanced defect-sink activity and vacancy annihilation. No quantitative results are recalled.
